categories: functional; security; privacy; regulatory; performance; availability_reliability; audit_reporting; operational_maintenance

statement: The system shall map them to applicable financial regulations, organisational policies, risk controls, and legacy-system constraints.
business_justification: To ensure that all requirements are aligned with relevant laws, internal guidelines, and existing systems.
acceptance_criteria: Requirements are mapped to at least 3 categories: financial regulations, organisational policies, risk controls, and legacy-system constraints.

statement: The system shall generate a justified, project-specific SDLC workflow with phases, activities, roles, deliverables, validation gates, security controls, and compliance checkpoints.
business_justification: To ensure that the development process is structured and aligned with best practices for software development in financial services.
acceptance_criteria: A project-specific SDLC workflow includes at least 5 phases: planning, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance.
applicable_regulations: Sample Audit, Retention & Regulatory Reporting Policy (fictional prototype document — not an authoritative regulatory source); Sample Credit Decisioning & Fair Lending Policy (fictional prototype document — not an authoritative regulatory source); Sample KYC & Customer Onboarding Policy (fictional prototype document — not an authoritative regulatory source)

statement: The system shall classify requirements into business requirements, stakeholder requirements, functional requirements, security requirements, privacy requirements, regulatory requirements, performance requirements, availability and reliability requirements, usability requirements, data-management requirements, integration requirements, audit and reporting requirements, operational and maintenance requirements.
categories: functional; security; privacy; regulatory; performance; availability_reliability; audit_reporting; operational_maintenance
business_justification: To ensure that all aspects of the requirements are categorized appropriately for proper development and testing.
acceptance_criteria: Requirements are classified into at least 13 categories: business requirements, stakeholder requirements, functional requirements, security requirements, privacy requirements, regulatory requirements, performance requirements, availability and reliability requirements, usability requirements, data-management requirements, integration requirements, audit and reporting requirements, operational and maintenance requirements.
applicable_regulations: Sample Audit, Retention & Regulatory Reporting Policy (fictional prototype document — not an authoritative regulatory source); Sample Data Privacy & Consent Policy (fictional prototype document — not an authoritative regulatory source)

statement: The system shall generate requirement artefacts such as Software Requirements Specification (SRS), user stories, use cases, acceptance criteria, compliance mappings, risk register, traceability matrix, and recommended SDLC model.
business_justification: To ensure that all requirements are documented in a structured format for review and approval by stakeholders and team members.
acceptance_criteria: Requirement artefacts include at least 7 types: Software Requirements Specification (SRS), user stories, use cases, acceptance criteria, compliance mappings, risk register, traceability matrix.

statement: The system shall derive project characteristics such as requirement stability, regulatory criticality, security risk, project complexity, system size, legacy-system dependence, frequency of expected changes, need for continuous delivery, availability of stakeholders, testing and documentation requirements, budget and schedule constraints, need for formal verification, consequences of system failure.
business_justification: To ensure that the selected SDLC approach is appropriate for the specific project needs.
acceptance_criteria: Project characteristics include at least 10 factors: requirement stability, regulatory criticality, security risk, project complexity, system size, legacy-system dependence, frequency of expected changes, need for continuous delivery, availability of stakeholders, testing and documentation requirements.

statement: The system shall generate a ranked recommendation for an appropriate Software Development Life Cycle model based on the derived project characteristics.
business_justification: To ensure that the selected SDLC approach is aligned with the specific needs of the project.
acceptance_criteria: A ranked recommendation includes at least 3 approaches: Waterfall, Agile, DevSecOps hybrid.

statement: The system shall customise the selected SDLC with development phases, activities within each phase, responsible roles, expected deliverables, security activities, testing requirements, compliance checkpoints, human-approval gates, entry and exit criteria, traceability requirements.
business_justification: To ensure that the development process is structured and aligned with best practices for software development in financial services.
acceptance_criteria: SDLC customisation includes at least 5 phases: planning, design, implementation, testing, maintenance.
applicable_regulations: Sample KYC & Customer Onboarding Policy (fictional prototype document — not an authoritative regulatory source)

statement: The system shall implement human-in-the-loop controls for final requirement baselines, regulatory interpretations, high-risk security requirements, conflicting stakeholder decisions, architecture-critical requirements, SDLC selection, changes to approved requirements, production-readiness decisions.
business_justification: To ensure that the development process is transparent and accountable, with human oversight where necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Human-in-the-loop controls include at least 5 types of approvals: final requirement baselines, regulatory interpretations, high-risk security requirements, conflicting stakeholder decisions, architecture-critical requirements.

statement: The system shall secure the Agentic AI platform with role-based access control, multi-factor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, sensitive-data masking, secure prompt and output filtering, agent-level permissions, retrieval-source allowlisting, protection against prompt injection, session isolation, audit logging, data-retention policies, model and knowledge-base versioning.
business_justification: To ensure that the development process is secure and compliant with relevant regulations.
acceptance_criteria: Platform security includes at least 10 controls: role-based access control, multi-factor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, sensitive-data masking, secure prompt and output filtering, agent-level permissions, retrieval-source allowlisting, protection against prompt injection, session isolation, audit logging.
